question: The revenue from selling $x$ units of a product is $R(x)=100x-x^2$ rupees. Find the marginal revenue when $40$ units are sold and determine whether the total revenue is increasing at that production level.
explanation: Marginal-revenue relationMarginal revenue is the derivative of total revenue with respect to the number of units sold.Differentiation$$MR=R'(x)=100-2x$$Evaluation at $x=40$$$MR=100-2(40)=20$$Interpretation of the derivativeSince the marginal revenue at $x=40$ is positive, the total revenue increases when the number of units sold increases near this production level.Final resultThe marginal revenue is ₹$20$ per additional unit. As $R'(40)>0$, the total revenue is increasing when $40$ units are sold.

options.A: ₹$60$ per additional unit; total revenue is increasing
options.B: ₹$20$ per additional unit; total revenue is increasing
options.C: ₹$20$ per additional unit; total revenue is decreasing
options.D: ₹$40$ per additional unit; total revenue is increasing
